apps/docs/blog/2026-05-28-why-blake3.mdx.line: On x86-64 with AVX-512, a single core can process four 1 KiB chunks simultaneously using 512-bit SIMD registers. On Apple Silicon (NEON 128-bit), two chunks per SIMD cycle. On WASM SIMD (128-bit), two chunks. On WASM without SIMD (scalar), one chunk per cycle — but the scalar ChaCha-derived loop is still simpler than SHA-256's schedule, so scalar BLAKE3 beats scalar SHA-256.

marketing/sales/FAQ-MASTER.md.line: **A:** Two cases. (1) **You cancel for convenience** (mid-annual-prepay): the refund posture is governed by the applicable agreement. (2) **For an SLA breach:** no service-credit program is currently active. If a future SLA becomes effective, its service credits are the sole remedy for covered breaches except for a valid termination under that SLA’s §8; a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees applies only on that valid termination and is not added again for the same breach. A material DPA breach is governed by the applicable executed DPA and agreement; this FAQ does not establish a separate refund entitlement. The audit-chain export is included free in either case — your data is yours, content-addressed, and portable by construction (you can leave any time; we are aware "BLAKE3 digests are content-addressed" is *itself* an escape hatch, see P34).

marketing/sales/FAQ-MASTER.md.line: **What a prospect may nonetheless see, stated precisely so we are never caught understating it:** a workflow named `.github/workflows/byok_kill_switch_drill_weekly.yml` **does exist, is on `cron: 0 3 * * 0`, and its 8 most recent runs (all `schedule`, 2026-07-05 → 2026-08-30) are green.** It proves nothing, because what it executes — `scripts/byok_kill_switch_drill.sh`, 181 lines of shell — **contacts no KMS, no CoreLink API, and no CoreLink binary at all** (every KMS credential in the job is commented out). Every asserted outcome is a shell literal: `TENANT_STATUS="active"` (`:51`), `DETECTED=true` (`:82`), `DEK_CACHE_EMPTY=true` (`:100`), `TENANT_STATUS_POST="degraded_read_only"` (`:101`), `RECOVERY_STATUS="active"` (`:129`). The "≤ 5 min" round-trip is `date +%s` taken before and after a `sleep 2` (`:62`, `:81`, `:112`). No assertion in it can be false, so the green is structurally inevitable, and no run has ever left evidence in the repo — the report step `git commit`s without `git push`, and `ls specs/_audits/ | grep -c byok-kill-switch-drill` returns **0**. These are the same **facts** the CAIQ `CEK-10.1` and SIG-LITE `N.6` carry — the wording is not identical across the three documents (`N.6` omits two of the shell literals, the CAIQ adds a code citation and a closing instruction, and only this FAQ states outright that the drill proves nothing), so cite the facts, not a shared sentence. Do not describe those facts any other way.

marketing/sales/legal-questionnaires/CAI.line: | CEK-10.1 | Kill-switch / key-revocation supported? | N | CSP | The `/deactivate` Shred route is implemented, but customer key revocation and the contractual kill-switch p99 have **no verified customer rollout**. `POST /v1/admin/byok/activate` fails closed with `501 Not Implemented` / `byok_not_available` if provider construction or CMK access fails (`crates/corelink-container/src/routes/byok_admin.rs:245-257`); the Dockerfile production build selects `byok-aws-real`, but customer CMK activation, revocation and kill-switch p99 lack runtime evidence. See CEK-09.1. **On the weekly drill, stated precisely, because the workflow is real but the drill is not:** `.github/workflows/byok_kill_switch_drill_weekly.yml` exists, is on `cron: 0 3 * * 0`, and its 8 most recent runs (all `schedule`, 2026-07-05 → 2026-08-30) are all `success`. What runs is `scripts/byok_kill_switch_drill.sh` (181 lines of shell), and **it is a shell simulation with the PASS values written into it as literals.** It contacts nothing: no customer KMS (every KMS credential in the job is commented out, `# AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: …`), no CoreLink API or D1 — and **not the compiled AWS KMS provider either**, because the script invokes no CoreLink binary at all. Every asserted outcome is a hard-coded assignment: `TENANT_STATUS="active"` (`:51`), `DETECTED=true` (`:82`), `DEK_CACHE_EMPTY=true` (`:100`), `TENANT_STATUS_POST="degraded_read_only"` (`:101`), `RECOVERY_STATUS="active"` (`:129`); the provider revoke/restore calls exist only as comments (`:64-67`, `:125`). The timing is `date +%s` taken before and after a `sleep 2` (`:62`, `:81`, `:112`), so **the `byok-kill-switch-rtt` "≤ 5 min" figure is a measurement of that sleep, not of any revocation**. Precisely: `DETECT_LATENCY_S` (`:75` → `:86`) and `TOTAL_S` (`:62` → `:112`) span the **same** single `sleep 2`, so the two reported numbers are not independent measurements; the two `sleep 1` calls (`:126`, `:128`) run after `:112` and fall outside both. And because no assertion can be false, the green result is structurally unfailable. No run has ever left evidence in the repo: the "Commit drill report" step of the workflow `git commit`s without `git push` (cited by step name, not line number, because the file shifts), and `specs/_audits/` contains **zero** `*-byok-kill-switch-drill-*.md` files. Treat the drill as unexecuted for assurance purposes. | C1.1 |

marketing/sales/legal-questionnaires/VEN.line: > **A:** CoreLink serves tenant-pinned R2/DO state through a **US (ENAM)** default path and a **physically-EU (WEUR)** path. EU (`weur`) CAS and AC blobs are stored in physically-EU Cloudflare R2 buckets (`corelink-cas-eu` / `corelink-ac-eu`, both EEUR) via London/`lhr`; this is an R2 residency statement. The D1 control plane is one shared global database, with its primary currently reported in ENAM and no D1 jurisdiction. The prelaunch DPA/TIA text does not establish an approved transfer basis or executed customer terms for that D1 posture. Other jurisdictions (`sam` São Paulo, `oce` Sydney, `apc` Tokyo/Singapore, `mea` Dubai) are roadmap items, not GA.
